title: Source-key matched BOLD runs show over 99.9% less disagreement in two accession families
abstract: We compared whole-run cortical median lag-one correlation across source-key matched ReadyNeuro runs and different-source-label pairings in the same protocols. Three V4 participants were discovery data. A frozen test used five narrative participants from an accession-disjoint source family. Mean shared-pair disagreement was 0.00001474 and 0.00002717, versus off-diagonal disagreement 0.03795775 and 0.03263924. Relative reductions were 99.961% and 99.917%. The held-out source pairing minimized disagreement over all 120 label permutations. Its conditional subject-bootstrap reduction interval was 99.544% to 99.962%. Seven of eight derivative arrays were byte-different. Four source-image downloads verified two raw source pairs against annex hashes. No common raw BOLD/T1 pointer blobs were found across source families. Source participant tables and a certified alias map were absent. This is a finite selected-scan measurement finding, not a corpus-wide bias estimate, causal reuse effect, or neural-activity claim. Person stability and exact-scan reuse remain inseparable here. Code, scalar features, plans, provenance and author reruns are included.
